Ravi @ Meharban vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 15 March,
2024
Author: Prem Narayan Singh

Bench: Prem Narayan Singh
 1
 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
 At Indore

 (Ravi @ Meharban Vs The State Of Madhya Prad
 Dated : 15-03-2024

entities.text:
High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
 At Indore
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Shri Samanway Sharma, learned counsel for the appellant.

Shri Sachin Jaiswal, learned Panel Lawyer for the respon Heard on I.A. No.5928/2023, which is first application under Section 389(1) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 for suspension of jail sentence and grant of bail filed on behalf of appellant No. 1 - Ravi.

T h e appellant has been convicted for the offence punishable under Section s 366A, 376(2)(n) and 376(2)(I) of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 and sentenced to undergo 07 years rigorous imprisonment,
10 years rigorous imprisonment and 10 years rigorous imprisonment along with fine of Rs.1,000/-,
Rs.2,000/- and Rs.2,000/- and default stipulations.
Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the appellant has already served more than half of the sentence i.e. almost 6 years out of 10 years.
Appellant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in the crime in question.
The age of the prosecutrix has not been properly established by the prosecution.
The Principal of the school Pramod Shukla (PW-5) has admitted in his cross-examination that the age of the prosecutrix was mentioned in the record only on the basis of her parents.
In this regard, statements of the parents prosecutrix are also significant wherein they are not sure about the age of prosecutrix.
The trial Court has not properly appreciated the oral and documentary evidence available on record.

The appellant is in jail and final disposal of this appeal would take considerable time to conclude, therefore, the custodial sentence of the appellant may be suspended and he may be released on bail.
Learned Govt. Advocate for the State has opposed the application.

Looking to the facts and circumstances of the case and mainly the fact that the appellant has already served more than half of the sentence, I deem it to be a fit case to suspend the custodial sentence of the appellant and to release him on bail, therefore, without commenting on the merits, this application is allowed.

I t is directed that subject to depositing the fine amount, if not already deposited and on furnishing a personal bond in a sum of Rs. 50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with one surety in the like Ravi @ Meharban vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 15 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/33323708/
1 amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court concerned, the custodial sentence of appellant shall remain suspended and he shall be released on bail for securing his presence before the Registry of this Court concerned on 22.08.2024 and on such other dates as may be fixed in this regard during pendency of this appeal.

sentences.text: The appellant shall regularly appear before the Registry of this Court on every date, without fail.
Accordingly, I.A. No.5928/2023 stands allowed and disposed of.
